title: The Kilkenny Hex

evidence.name: Torn Order Pad
evidence.text: Under the plinth: a sheet from a green-lined order pad, 'BACK BY SUNDAY, SORRY!' in a rush, a tea ring and a smell of leeks. Half of Kilkenny's kitchens use that pad.

evidence.name: Trolley Tracks
evidence.text: Two thin wheel tracks and a smear of grease out of the back door and into the Butter Slip, the narrow lane to the High Street. Whoever it was had a hand trolley, and a squeaky wheel.

evidence.name: Visitors' Book
evidence.text: Rothe House's night book: Declan the steward signed the Tudor Garden evening in at seven and out at midnight, with sixty witnesses and an orchard of apples. He was here the whole time.

evidence.name: Soup Tent Permit
evidence.text: The Tholsel stamped a permit for the Hurling Museum's soup tent. Applicant: the Butter Slip Cafe. Equipment: 'one 60-litre iron pot, to be sourced'. Underlined twice.

evidence.name: Soup Tent Notice
evidence.text: The Hurling Museum is running a soup tent for Sunday's final and wants 'big pots, 60 litres a go'. The permits are done at the Tholsel.

evidence.name: Declan's Letter
evidence.text: A letter from Rothe House offering Nuala a handsome sum for 'an authentic Kyteler artefact'. Declan is very keen. He is also very polite, and has not been near the inn since.

evidence.name: Muddy Cloak
evidence.text: The verger's black cloak hem is muddy and he was seen outside the inn at midnight. He lights a candle on the doorstep every year for Petronilla, burnt in 1324. He did not take the pot.

suspects.name: Declan Fitzpatrick
suspects.wrong: I wrote a letter, not a ransom note! I was signed in at Rothe House all night, there is a book! I shall be writing to the Heritage Council. In Latin.

suspects.name: Verger Mooney
suspects.wrong: A candle for Petronilla is not a crime, I'll have you know. It is the only thing the Church has done for her in seven hundred years. I think you should go and apologise to somebody.

suspects.name: Clerk Brennan
suspects.wrong: I stamp. That is what I do. I stamped for a tent, not a heist. The stamp is not a suspect. I am not a suspect. Form 14B for apologies, in triplicate.

suspects.name: Maeve Dunne
suspects.right: Ah, would you stop. The hurling soup tent wanted sixty litres and my pot cracked on Thursday. I was going to put it back Monday and I left a note! It must have blown off the plinth. I'll bring it back myself, scrubbed. And there's soup in it for the whole town. Sorry, Nuala.

steps.text: Speak to Nuala, the landlady of Kyteler's Inn, Kilkenny.
Look at the empty hook and plinth by the hearth in Kyteler's.
Check the back door at Kyteler's for marks.
Question Declan, the steward of Rothe House.
Look at the visitors' book in Rothe House.
Question the verger at St Canice's Cathedral.
Ask the clerk at the Tholsel about permits.
Read the notice at the Hurling Museum.
Look at the kitchen door of the Butter Slip Cafe.
Report back to Nuala at Kyteler's Inn.

accuse_hint: Nuala is waiting at Kyteler's Inn.
closed: Petronilla's pot is back on its hook, scrubbed, and the hurling soup tent sold out by half one.
